reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Calling acquired tonsillar descent from low CSF pressure a Chiari I malformation.
name: Chiari Malformation Classification

version.label: Classical Chiari types I–IV (Chiari 1891, 1896)
version.detail: Types 0, 1.5 and V are later additions and are not included. The ≥5 mm tonsillar descent threshold is a later radiological convention.

intendedPopulation: Patients with posterior fossa or craniovertebral junction anomalies on MRI.

options.label: Type I: Caudal displacement of the cerebellar tonsils below the foramen magnum (commonly ≥5 mm on MRI)
Type II: Caudal displacement of the vermis, brainstem and fourth ventricle
Type III: Herniation of posterior fossa contents into a low occipital or high cervical encephalocele
Type IV: Severe cerebellar hypoplasia without herniation

resultStates.label: Type I
resultStates.summary: Caudal displacement of the cerebellar tonsils below the foramen magnum (commonly ≥5 mm on MRI).

resultStates.label: Type II
resultStates.summary: Caudal displacement of the vermis, brainstem and fourth ventricle.
resultStates.detail: Almost always with open spinal dysraphism (myelomeningocele).

resultStates.label: Type III
resultStates.summary: Herniation of posterior fossa contents into a low occipital or high cervical encephalocele.

resultStates.label: Type IV
resultStates.detail: Now regarded as a form of cerebellar hypoplasia.

clinicalContext.text: Types I and II are common in clinical practice; type II accompanies myelomeningocele.

clinicalInsights.text: Tonsillar descent alone, without symptoms or syrinx, is often an incidental finding.

limitations.text: Anatomical classification; symptoms correlate poorly with the degree of tonsillar descent.

limitations: Types IV and later additions are inconsistently defined between sources.
whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether symptoms are due to the malformation.

guideSections.what: Four classical types of hindbrain malformation.
guideSections.whenToUse: MRI of the posterior fossa and craniovertebral junction.
guideSections.howToPerform: Identify which structures are displaced and any associated dysraphism or encephalocele.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Correlate with symptoms, syrinx and CSF flow.

sources.citation: Chiari H. Über Veränderungen des Kleinhirns infolge von Hydrocephalie des Grosshirns. Dtsch Med Wochenschr. 1891;17:1172-1175.
